S0001.name: Trojan.Mebromi
S0001.summary: Trojan.Mebromi is BIOS-level malware that takes control of the victim before MBR.

S0002.name: Mimikatz
S0002.summary: Mimikatz is a credential dumper capable of obtaining plaintext Windows account logins and passwords, along with many other features that make it useful for testing the security of networks.

S0003.name: RIPTIDE
S0003.summary: RIPTIDE is a proxy-aware backdoor used by APT12.

S0004.name: TinyZBot
S0004.summary: TinyZBot is a bot written in C# that was developed by Cleaver.

S0005.name: Windows Credential Editor
S0005.summary: Windows Credential Editor is a password dumping tool.

S0007.name: Skeleton Key
S0007.summary: Skeleton Key is malware used to inject false credentials into domain controllers with the intent of creating a backdoor password. Functionality similar to Skeleton Key is included as a module in Mimikatz.

S0008.name: gsecdump
S0008.summary: gsecdump is a publicly-available credential dumper used to obtain password hashes and LSA secrets from Windows operating systems.

S0009.name: Hikit
S0009.summary: Hikit is malware that has been used by Axiom for late-stage persistence and exfiltration after the initial compromise.

S0010.name: Lurid
S0010.summary: Lurid is a malware family that has been used by several groups, including PittyTiger, in targeted attacks as far back as 2006.

S0011.name: Taidoor
S0011.summary: Taidoor is a remote access trojan (RAT) that has been used by Chinese government cyber actors to maintain access on victim networks. Taidoor has primarily been used against Taiwanese government organizations since at least 2010.

S0012.name: PoisonIvy
S0012.summary: PoisonIvy is a popular remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by many groups.

S0013.name: PlugX
S0013.summary: PlugX is a remote access tool (RAT) with modular plugins that has been used by multiple threat groups.

S0014.name: BS2005
S0014.summary: BS2005 is malware that was used by Ke3chang in spearphishing campaigns since at least 2011.

S0015.name: Ixeshe
S0015.summary: Ixeshe is a malware family that has been used since at least 2009 against targets in East Asia.

S0016.name: P2P ZeuS
S0016.summary: P2P ZeuS is a closed-source fork of the leaked version of the ZeuS botnet. It presents improvements over the leaked version, including a peer-to-peer architecture.

S0017.name: BISCUIT
S0017.summary: BISCUIT is a backdoor that has been used by APT1 since as early as 2007.

S0018.name: Sykipot
S0018.summary: Sykipot is malware that has been used in spearphishing campaigns since approximately 2007 against victims primarily in the US. One variant of Sykipot hijacks smart cards on victims. The group using this malware has also been referred to as Sykipot.

S0019.name: Regin
S0019.summary: Regin is a malware platform that has targeted victims in a range of industries, including telecom, government, and financial institutions. Some Regin timestamps date back to 2003.

S0020.name: China Chopper
S0020.summary: China Chopper is a Web Shell hosted on Web servers to provide access back into an enterprise network that does not rely on an infected system calling back to a remote command and control server. It has been used by several threat groups.

S0021.name: Derusbi
S0021.summary: Derusbi is malware used by multiple Chinese APT groups. Both Windows and Linux variants have been observed.

S0022.name: Uroburos
S0022.summary: Uroburos is a sophisticated cyber espionage tool written in C that has been used by units within Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) associated with the Turla toolset to collect intelligence on sensitive targets worldwide. Uroburos has several variants and has undergone nearly constant upgrade since its initial development in 2003 to keep it viable after public disclosures.

S0023.name: CHOPSTICK
S0023.summary: CHOPSTICK is a malware family of modular backdoors used by APT28. It has been used since at least 2012 and is usually dropped on victims as second-stage malware, though it has been used as first-stage malware in several cases. It has both Windows and Linux variants. It is tracked separately from the X-Agent for Android.

S0024.name: Dyre
S0024.summary: Dyre is a banking Trojan that has been used for financial gain.

S0025.name: CALENDAR
S0025.summary: CALENDAR is malware used by APT1 that mimics legitimate Gmail Calendar traffic.

S0026.name: GLOOXMAIL
S0026.summary: GLOOXMAIL is malware used by APT1 that mimics legitimate Jabber/XMPP traffic.

S0027.name: Zeroaccess
S0027.summary: Zeroaccess is a kernel-mode Rootkit that attempts to add victims to the ZeroAccess botnet, often for monetary gain.

S0028.name: SHIPSHAPE
S0028.summary: SHIPSHAPE is malware developed by APT30 that allows propagation and exfiltration of data over removable devices. APT30 may use this capability to exfiltrate data across air-gaps.

S0029.name: PsExec
S0029.summary: PsExec is a free Microsoft tool that can be used to execute a program on another computer. It is used by IT administrators and attackers.

S0030.name: Carbanak
S0030.summary: Carbanak is a full-featured, remote backdoor used by a group of the same name (Carbanak). It is intended for espionage, data exfiltration, and providing remote access to infected machines.

S0031.name: BACKSPACE
S0031.summary: BACKSPACE is a backdoor used by APT30 that dates back to at least 2005.

S0032.name: gh0st RAT
S0032.summary: gh0st RAT is a remote access tool (RAT). The source code is public and it has been used by multiple groups.

S0033.name: NetTraveler
S0033.summary: NetTraveler is malware that has been used in multiple cyber espionage campaigns for basic surveillance of victims. The earliest known samples have timestamps back to 2005, and the largest number of observed samples were created between 2010 and 2013.

S0034.name: NETEAGLE
S0034.summary: NETEAGLE is a backdoor developed by APT30 with compile dates as early as 2008. It has two main variants known as “Scout” and “Norton.”

S0035.name: SPACESHIP
S0035.summary: SPACESHIP is malware developed by APT30 that allows propagation and exfiltration of data over removable devices. APT30 may use this capability to exfiltrate data across air-gaps.

S0036.name: FLASHFLOOD
S0036.summary: FLASHFLOOD is malware developed by APT30 that allows propagation and exfiltration of data over removable devices. APT30 may use this capability to exfiltrate data across air-gaps.

S0037.name: HAMMERTOSS
S0037.summary: HAMMERTOSS is a backdoor that was used by APT29 in 2015.

S0038.name: Duqu
S0038.summary: Duqu is a malware platform that uses a modular approach to extend functionality after deployment within a target network.

S0039.name: Net
S0039.summary: The Net utility is a component of the Windows operating system. It is used in command-line operations for control of users, groups, services, and network connections.

S0040.name: HTRAN
S0040.summary: HTRAN is a tool that proxies connections through intermediate hops and aids users in disguising their true geographical location. It can be used by adversaries to hide their location when interacting with the victim networks.

S0041.name: Wiper
S0041.summary: Wiper is a family of destructive malware used in March 2013 during breaches of South Korean banks and media companies.

S0042.name: LOWBALL
S0042.summary: LOWBALL is malware used by admin@338. It was used in August 2015 in email messages targeting Hong Kong-based media organizations.

S0043.name: BUBBLEWRAP
S0043.summary: BUBBLEWRAP is a full-featured, second-stage backdoor used by the admin@338 group. It is set to run when the system boots and includes functionality to check, upload, and register plug-ins that can further enhance its capabilities.

S0044.name: JHUHUGIT
S0044.summary: JHUHUGIT is malware used by APT28. It is based on Carberp source code and serves as reconnaissance malware.

S0045.name: ADVSTORESHELL
S0045.summary: ADVSTORESHELL is a spying backdoor that has been used by APT28 from at least 2012 to 2016. It is generally used for long-term espionage and is deployed on targets deemed interesting after a reconnaissance phase.

S0046.name: CozyCar
S0046.summary: CozyCar is malware that was used by APT29 from 2010 to 2015. It is a modular malware platform, and its backdoor component can be instructed to download and execute a variety of modules with different functionality.

S0047.name: Hacking Team UEFI Rootkit
S0047.summary: Hacking Team UEFI Rootkit is a rootkit developed by the company Hacking Team as a method of persistence for remote access software.

S0048.name: PinchDuke
S0048.summary: PinchDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2008 to 2010.

S0049.name: GeminiDuke
S0049.summary: GeminiDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2009 to 2012.

S0050.name: CosmicDuke
S0050.summary: CosmicDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2010 to 2015.

S0051.name: MiniDuke
S0051.summary: MiniDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2010 to 2015. The MiniDuke toolset consists of multiple downloader and backdoor components. The loader has been used with other MiniDuke components as well as in conjunction with CosmicDuke and PinchDuke.

S0052.name: OnionDuke
S0052.summary: OnionDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2013 to 2015.

S0053.name: SeaDuke
S0053.summary: SeaDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2014 to 2015. It was used primarily as a secondary backdoor for victims that were already compromised with CozyCar.

S0054.name: CloudDuke
S0054.summary: CloudDuke is malware that was used by APT29 in 2015.

S0055.name: RARSTONE
S0055.summary: RARSTONE is malware used by the Naikon group that has some characteristics similar to PlugX.

S0056.name: Net Crawler
S0056.summary: Net Crawler is an intranet worm capable of extracting credentials using credential dumpers and spreading to systems on a network over SMB by brute forcing accounts with recovered passwords and using PsExec to execute a copy of Net Crawler.

S0057.name: Tasklist
S0057.summary: The Tasklist utility displays a list of applications and services with their Process IDs (PID) for all tasks running on either a local or a remote computer. It is packaged with Windows operating systems and can be executed from the command-line interface.

S0058.name: SslMM
S0058.summary: SslMM is a full-featured backdoor used by Naikon that has multiple variants.

S0059.name: WinMM
S0059.summary: WinMM is a full-featured, simple backdoor used by Naikon.

S0060.name: Sys10
S0060.summary: Sys10 is a backdoor that was used throughout 2013 by Naikon.

S0061.name: HDoor
S0061.summary: HDoor is malware that has been customized and used by the Naikon group.

S0062.name: DustySky
S0062.summary: DustySky is multi-stage malware written in .NET that has been used by Molerats since May 2015.

S0063.name: SHOTPUT
S0063.summary: SHOTPUT is a custom backdoor used by APT3.

S0064.name: ELMER
S0064.summary: ELMER is a non-persistent, proxy-aware HTTP backdoor written in Delphi that has been used by APT16.

S0065.name: 4H RAT
S0065.summary: 4H RAT is malware that has been used by Putter Panda since at least 2007.

S0066.name: 3PARA RAT
S0066.summary: 3PARA RAT is a remote access tool (RAT) programmed in C++ that has been used by Putter Panda.

S0067.name: pngdowner
S0067.summary: pngdowner is malware used by Putter Panda. It is a simple tool with limited functionality and no persistence mechanism, suggesting it is used only as a simple "download-and-

S0068.name: httpclient
S0068.summary: httpclient is malware used by Putter Panda. It is a simple tool that provides a limited range of functionality, suggesting it is likely used as a second-stage or supplementary/backup tool.

S0069.name: BLACKCOFFEE
S0069.summary: BLACKCOFFEE is malware that has been used by several Chinese groups since at least 2013.

S0070.name: HTTPBrowser
S0070.summary: HTTPBrowser is malware that has been used by several threat groups. It is believed to be of Chinese origin.

S0071.name: hcdLoader
S0071.summary: hcdLoader is a remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by APT18.

S0072.name: OwaAuth
S0072.summary: OwaAuth is a Web shell and credential stealer deployed to Microsoft Exchange servers that appears to be exclusively used by Threat Group-3390.

S0073.name: ASPXSpy
S0073.summary: ASPXSpy is a Web shell. It has been modified by Threat Group-3390 actors to create the ASPXTool version.

S0074.name: Sakula
S0074.summary: Sakula is a remote access tool (RAT) that first surfaced in 2012 and was used in intrusions throughout 2015.

S0075.name: Reg
S0075.summary: Reg is a Windows utility used to interact with the Windows Registry. It can be used at the command-line interface to query, add, modify, and remove information.

S0076.name: FakeM
S0076.summary: FakeM is a shellcode-based Windows backdoor that has been used by Scarlet Mimic.

S0077.name: CallMe
S0077.summary: CallMe is a Trojan designed to run on Apple OSX. It is based on a publicly available tool called Tiny SHell.

S0078.name: Psylo
S0078.summary: Psylo is a shellcode-based Trojan that has been used by Scarlet Mimic. It has similar characteristics as FakeM.

S0079.name: MobileOrder
S0079.summary: MobileOrder is a Trojan intended to compromise Android mobile devices. It has been used by Scarlet Mimic.

S0080.name: Mivast
S0080.summary: Mivast is a backdoor that has been used by Deep Panda. It was reportedly used in the Anthem breach.

S0081.name: Elise
S0081.summary: Elise is a custom backdoor Trojan that appears to be used exclusively by Lotus Blossom. It is part of a larger group of tools referred to as LStudio, ST Group, and APT0LSTU.

S0082.name: Emissary
S0082.summary: Emissary is a Trojan that has been used by Lotus Blossom. It shares code with Elise, with both Trojans being part of a malware group referred to as LStudio.

S0083.name: Misdat
S0083.summary: Misdat is a backdoor that was used in Operation Dust Storm from 2010 to 2011.

S0084.name: Mis-Type
S0084.summary: Mis-Type is a backdoor hybrid that was used in Operation Dust Storm by 2012.

S0085.name: S-Type
S0085.summary: S-Type is a backdoor that was used in Operation Dust Storm since at least 2013.

S0086.name: ZLib
S0086.summary: ZLib is a full-featured backdoor that was used as a second-stage implant during Operation Dust Storm since at least 2014. ZLib is malware and should not be confused with the legitimate compression library from which its name is derived.

S0087.name: Hi-Zor
S0087.summary: Hi-Zor is a remote access tool (RAT) that has characteristics similar to Sakula. It was used in a campaign named INOCNATION.

S0088.name: Kasidet
S0088.summary: Kasidet is a backdoor that has been dropped by using malicious VBA macros.

S0089.name: BlackEnergy
S0089.summary: BlackEnergy is a malware toolkit that has been used by both criminal and APT actors. It dates back to at least 2007 and was originally designed to create botnets for use in conducting Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, but its use has evolved to support various plug-ins.

S0090.name: Rover
S0090.summary: Rover is malware suspected of being used for espionage purposes. It was used in 2015 in a targeted email sent to an Indian Ambassador to Afghanistan.

S0091.name: Epic
S0091.summary: Epic is a backdoor that has been used by Turla.

S0092.name: Agent.btz
S0092.summary: Agent.btz is a worm that primarily spreads itself via removable devices such as USB drives. It reportedly infected U.S. military networks in 2008.

S0093.name: Backdoor.Oldrea
S0093.summary: Backdoor.Oldrea is a modular backdoor that used by Dragonfly against energy companies since at least 2013. Backdoor.Oldrea was distributed via supply chain compromise, and included specialized modules to enumerate and map ICS-specific systems, processes, and protocols.

S0094.name: Trojan.Karagany
S0094.summary: Trojan.Karagany is a modular remote access tool used for recon and linked to Dragonfly. The source code for Trojan.Karagany originated from Dream Loader malware which was leaked in 2010 and sold on underground forums.

S0095.name: ftp
S0095.summary: ftp is a utility commonly available with operating systems to transfer information over the File Transfer Protocol (FTP). Adversaries can use it to transfer other tools onto a system or to exfiltrate data.

S0096.name: Systeminfo
S0096.summary: Systeminfo is a Windows utility that can be used to gather detailed information about a computer.

S0097.name: Ping
S0097.summary: Ping is an operating system utility commonly used to troubleshoot and verify network connections.

S0098.name: T9000
S0098.summary: T9000 is a backdoor that is a newer variant of the T5000 malware family, also known as Plat1. Its primary function is to gather information about the victim. It has been used in multiple targeted attacks against U.S.-based organizations.

S0099.name: Arp
S0099.summary: Arp displays and modifies information about a system's Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) cache.

S0100.name: ipconfig
S0100.summary: ipconfig is a Windows utility that can be used to find information about a system's TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and adapter configuration.

S0101.name: ifconfig
S0101.summary: ifconfig is a Unix-based utility used to gather information about and interact with the TCP/IP settings on a system.

S0102.name: nbtstat
S0102.summary: nbtstat is a utility used to troubleshoot NetBIOS name resolution.

S0103.name: route
S0103.summary: route can be used to find or change information within the local system IP routing table.

S0104.name: netstat
S0104.summary: netstat is an operating system utility that displays active TCP connections, listening ports, and network statistics.

S0105.name: dsquery
S0105.summary: dsquery is a command-line utility that can be used to query Active Directory for information from a system within a domain. It is typically installed only on Windows Server versions but can be installed on non-server variants through the Microsoft-provided Remote Server Administration Tools bundle.

S0106.name: cmd
S0106.summary: cmd is the Windows command-line interpreter that can be used to interact with systems and execute other processes and utilities.

S0107.name: Cherry Picker
S0107.summary: Cherry Picker is a point of sale (PoS) memory scraper.

S0108.name: netsh
S0108.summary: netsh is a scripting utility used to interact with networking components on local or remote systems.

S0109.name: WEBC2
S0109.summary: WEBC2 is a family of backdoor malware used by APT1 as early as July 2006. WEBC2 backdoors are designed to retrieve a webpage, with commands hidden in HTML comments or special tags, from a predetermined C2 server.

S0110.name: at
S0110.summary: at is used to schedule tasks on a system to run at a specified date or time.

S0111.name: schtasks
S0111.summary: schtasks is used to schedule execution of programs or scripts on a Windows system to run at a specific date and time.

S0112.name: ROCKBOOT
S0112.summary: ROCKBOOT is a Bootkit that has been used by an unidentified, suspected China-based group.

S0113.name: Prikormka
S0113.summary: Prikormka is a malware family used in a campaign known as Operation Groundbait. It has predominantly been observed in Ukraine and was used as early as 2008.

S0114.name: BOOTRASH
S0114.summary: BOOTRASH is a Bootkit that targets Windows operating systems. It has been used by threat actors that target the financial sector.

S0115.name: Crimson
S0115.summary: Crimson is a remote access Trojan that has been used by Transparent Tribe since at least 2016.

S0116.name: UACMe
S0116.summary: UACMe is an open source assessment tool that contains many methods for bypassing Windows User Account Control on multiple versions of the operating system.

S0117.name: XTunnel
S0117.summary: XTunnel a VPN-like network proxy tool that can relay traffic between a C2 server and a victim. It was first seen in May 2013 and reportedly used by APT28 during the compromise of the Democratic National Committee.

S0118.name: Nidiran
S0118.summary: Nidiran is a custom backdoor developed and used by Suckfly. It has been delivered via strategic web compromise.

S0119.name: Cachedump
S0119.summary: Cachedump is a publicly-available tool that program extracts cached password hashes from a system’s registry.

S0120.name: Fgdump
S0120.summary: Fgdump is a Windows password hash dumper.

S0121.name: Lslsass
S0121.summary: Lslsass is a publicly-available tool that can dump active logon session password hashes from the lsass process.

S0122.name: Pass-The-Hash Toolkit
S0122.summary: Pass-The-Hash Toolkit is a toolkit that allows an adversary to "pass" a password hash (without knowing the original password) to log in to systems.

S0123.name: xCmd
S0123.summary: xCmd is an open source tool that is similar to PsExec and allows the user to execute applications on remote systems.

S0124.name: Pisloader
S0124.summary: Pisloader is a malware family that is notable due to its use of DNS as a C2 protocol as well as its use of anti-analysis tactics. It has been used by APT18 and is similar to another malware family, HTTPBrowser, that has been used by the group.

S0125.name: Remsec
S0125.summary: Remsec is a modular backdoor that has been used by Strider and appears to have been designed primarily for espionage purposes. Many of its modules are written in Lua.

S0126.name: ComRAT
S0126.summary: ComRAT is a second stage implant suspected of being a descendant of Agent.btz and used by Turla. The first version of ComRAT was identified in 2007, but the tool has undergone substantial development for many years since.

S0127.name: BBSRAT
S0127.summary: BBSRAT is malware with remote access tool functionality that has been used in targeted compromises.

S0128.name: BADNEWS
S0128.summary: BADNEWS is malware that has been used by the actors responsible for the Patchwork campaign. Its name was given due to its use of RSS feeds, forums, and blogs for command and control.

S0129.name: AutoIt backdoor
S0129.summary: AutoIt backdoor is malware that has been used by the actors responsible for the MONSOON campaign. The actors frequently used it in weaponized .pps files exploiting CVE-2014-6352. This malware makes use of the legitimate scripting language for Windows GUI automation with the same name.

S0130.name: Unknown Logger
S0130.summary: Unknown Logger is a publicly released, free backdoor. Version 1.5 of the backdoor has been used by the actors responsible for the MONSOON campaign.

S0131.name: TINYTYPHON
S0131.summary: TINYTYPHON is a backdoor that has been used by the actors responsible for the MONSOON campaign. The majority of its code was reportedly taken from the MyDoom worm.

S0132.name: H1N1
S0132.summary: H1N1 is a malware variant that has been distributed via a campaign using VBA macros to infect victims. Although it initially had only loader capabilities, it has evolved to include information-stealing functionality.

S0133.name: Miner-C
S0133.summary: Miner-C is malware that mines victims for the Monero cryptocurrency. It has targeted FTP servers and Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices to spread.

S0134.name: Downdelph
S0134.summary: Downdelph is a first-stage downloader written in Delphi that has been used by APT28 in rare instances between 2013 and 2015.

S0135.name: HIDEDRV
S0135.summary: HIDEDRV is a rootkit used by APT28. It has been deployed along with Downdelph to execute and hide that malware.

S0136.name: USBStealer
S0136.summary: USBStealer is malware that has been used by APT28 since at least 2005 to extract information from air-gapped networks. It does not have the capability to communicate over the Internet and has been used in conjunction with ADVSTORESHELL.

S0137.name: CORESHELL
S0137.summary: CORESHELL is a downloader used by APT28. The older versions of this malware are known as SOURFACE and newer versions as CORESHELL.

S0138.name: OLDBAIT
S0138.summary: OLDBAIT is a credential harvester used by APT28.

S0139.name: PowerDuke
S0139.summary: PowerDuke is a backdoor that was used by APT29 in 2016. It has primarily been delivered through Microsoft Word or Excel attachments containing malicious macros.

S0140.name: Shamoon
S0140.summary: Shamoon is wiper malware that was first used by an Iranian group known as the "Cutting Sword of Justice" in 2012. Other versions known as Shamoon 2 and Shamoon 3 were observed in 2016 and 2018. Shamoon has also been seen leveraging RawDisk and Filerase to carry out data wiping tasks. Analysis has linked Shamoon with Kwampirs based on multiple shared artifacts and coding patterns.

S0141.name: Winnti for Windows
S0141.summary: Winnti for Windows is a modular remote access Trojan (RAT) that has been used likely by multiple groups to carry out intrusions in various regions since at least 2010, including by one group referred to as the same name, Winnti Group.. The Linux variant is tracked separately under Winnti for Linux.

S0142.name: StreamEx
S0142.summary: StreamEx is a malware family that has been used by Deep Panda since at least 2015. In 2016, it was distributed via legitimate compromised Korean websites.

S0143.name: Flame
S0143.summary: Flame is a sophisticated toolkit that has been used to collect information since at least 2010, largely targeting Middle East countries.

S0144.name: ChChes
S0144.summary: ChChes is a Trojan that appears to be used exclusively by menuPass. It was used to target Japanese organizations in 2016. Its lack of persistence methods suggests it may be intended as a first-stage tool.

S0145.name: POWERSOURCE
S0145.summary: POWERSOURCE is a PowerShell backdoor that is a heavily obfuscated and modified version of the publicly available tool DNS_TXT_Pwnage. It was observed in February 2017 in spearphishing campaigns against personnel involved with United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings at various organizations. The malware was delivered when macros were enabled by the victim and a VBS script was dropped.

S0146.name: TEXTMATE
S0146.summary: TEXTMATE is a second-stage PowerShell backdoor that is memory-resident. It was observed being used along with POWERSOURCE in February 2017.

S0147.name: Pteranodon
S0147.summary: Pteranodon is a custom backdoor used by Gamaredon Group.

S0148.name: RTM
S0148.summary: RTM is custom malware written in Delphi. It is used by the group of the same name (RTM). Newer versions of the malware have been reported publicly as Redaman.

S0149.name: MoonWind
S0149.summary: MoonWind is a remote access tool (RAT) that was used in 2016 to target organizations in Thailand.

S0150.name: POSHSPY
S0150.summary: POSHSPY is a backdoor that has been used by APT29 since at least 2015. It appears to be used as a secondary backdoor used if the actors lost access to their primary backdoors.

S0151.name: HALFBAKED
S0151.summary: HALFBAKED is a malware family consisting of multiple components intended to establish persistence in victim networks.

S0152.name: EvilGrab
S0152.summary: EvilGrab is a malware family with common reconnaissance capabilities. It has been deployed by menuPass via malicious Microsoft Office documents as part of spearphishing campaigns.

S0153.name: RedLeaves
S0153.summary: RedLeaves is a malware family used by menuPass. The code overlaps with PlugX and may be based upon the open source tool Trochilus.

S0154.name: Cobalt Strike
S0154.summary: Cobalt Strike is a commercial, full-featured, remote access tool that bills itself as “adversary simulation software designed to execute targeted attacks and emulate the post-exploitation actions of advanced threat actors”. Cobalt Strike’s interactive post-exploit capabilities cover the full range of ATT&CK tactics, all executed within a single, integrated system.

S0155.name: WINDSHIELD
S0155.summary: WINDSHIELD is a signature backdoor used by APT32.

S0156.name: KOMPROGO
S0156.summary: KOMPROGO is a signature backdoor used by APT32 that is capable of process, file, and registry management.

S0157.name: SOUNDBITE
S0157.summary: SOUNDBITE is a signature backdoor used by APT32.

S0158.name: PHOREAL
S0158.summary: PHOREAL is a signature backdoor used by APT32.

S0159.name: SNUGRIDE
S0159.summary: SNUGRIDE is a backdoor that has been used by menuPass as first stage malware.

S0160.name: certutil
S0160.summary: certutil is a command-line utility that can be used to obtain certificate authority information and configure Certificate Services.

S0161.name: XAgentOSX
S0161.summary: XAgentOSX is a trojan that has been used by APT28 on OS X and appears to be a port of their standard CHOPSTICK or XAgent trojan.

S0162.name: Komplex
S0162.summary: Komplex is a backdoor that has been used by APT28 on OS X and appears to be developed in a similar manner to XAgentOSX .

S0163.name: Janicab
S0163.summary: Janicab is an OS X trojan that relied on a valid developer ID and oblivious users to install it.

S0164.name: TDTESS
S0164.summary: TDTESS is a 64-bit .NET binary backdoor used by CopyKittens.

S0165.name: OSInfo
S0165.summary: OSInfo is a custom tool used by APT3 to do internal discovery on a victim's computer and network.

S0166.name: RemoteCMD
S0166.summary: RemoteCMD is a custom tool used by APT3 to execute commands on a remote system similar to SysInternal's PSEXEC functionality.

S0167.name: Matryoshka
S0167.summary: Matryoshka is a malware framework used by CopyKittens that consists of a dropper, loader, and RAT. It has multiple versions; v1 was seen in the wild from July 2016 until January 2017. v2 has fewer commands and other minor differences.

S0168.name: Gazer
S0168.summary: Gazer is a backdoor used by Turla since at least 2016.

S0169.name: RawPOS
S0169.summary: RawPOS is a point-of-sale (POS) malware family that searches for cardholder data on victims. It has been in use since at least 2008. FireEye divides RawPOS into three components: FIENDCRY, DUEBREW, and DRIFTWOOD.

S0170.name: Helminth
S0170.summary: Helminth is a backdoor that has at least two variants - one written in VBScript and PowerShell that is delivered via a macros in Excel spreadsheets, and one that is a standalone Windows executable.

S0171.name: Felismus
S0171.summary: Felismus is a modular backdoor that has been used by Sowbug.

S0172.name: Reaver
S0172.summary: Reaver is a malware family that has been in the wild since at least late 2016. Reporting indicates victims have primarily been associated with the "Five Poisons," which are movements the Chinese government considers dangerous. The type of malware is rare due to its final payload being in the form of Control Panel items.

S0173.name: FLIPSIDE
S0173.summary: FLIPSIDE is a simple tool similar to Plink that is used by FIN5 to maintain access to victims.

S0174.name: Responder
S0174.summary: Responder is an open source tool used for LLMNR, NBT-NS and MDNS poisoning, with built-in HTTP/SMB/MSSQL/FTP/LDAP rogue authentication server supporting NTLMv1/NTLMv2/LMv2, Extended Security NTLMSSP and Basic HTTP authentication.

S0175.name: meek
S0175.summary: meek is an open-source Tor plugin that tunnels Tor traffic through HTTPS connections.

S0176.name: Wingbird
S0176.summary: Wingbird is a backdoor that appears to be a version of commercial software FinFisher. It is reportedly used to attack individual computers instead of networks. It was used by NEODYMIUM in a May 2016 campaign.

S0177.name: Power Loader
S0177.summary: Power Loader is modular code sold in the cybercrime market used as a downloader in malware families such as Carberp, Redyms and Gapz.

S0178.name: Truvasys
S0178.summary: Truvasys is first-stage malware that has been used by PROMETHIUM. It is a collection of modules written in the Delphi programming language.

S0179.name: MimiPenguin
S0179.summary: MimiPenguin is a credential dumper, similar to Mimikatz, designed specifically for Linux platforms.

S0180.name: Volgmer
S0180.summary: Volgmer is a backdoor Trojan designed to provide covert access to a compromised system. It has been used since at least 2013 to target the government, financial, automotive, and media industries. Its primary delivery mechanism is suspected to be spearphishing.

S0181.name: FALLCHILL
S0181.summary: FALLCHILL is a RAT that has been used by Lazarus Group since at least 2016 to target the aerospace, telecommunications, and finance industries. It is usually dropped by other Lazarus Group malware or delivered when a victim unknowingly visits a compromised website.

S0182.name: FinFisher
S0182.summary: FinFisher is a government-grade commercial surveillance spyware reportedly sold exclusively to government agencies for use in targeted and lawful criminal investigations. It is heavily obfuscated and uses multiple anti-analysis techniques. It has other variants including Wingbird.

S0183.name: Tor
S0183.summary: Tor is a software suite and network that provides increased anonymity on the Internet. It creates a multi-hop proxy network and utilizes multilayer encryption to protect both the message and routing information. Tor utilizes "Onion Routing," in which messages are encrypted with multiple layers of encryption; at each step in the proxy network, the topmost layer is decrypted and the contents forwarded on to the next no…

S0184.name: POWRUNER
S0184.summary: POWRUNER is a PowerShell script that sends and receives commands to and from the C2 server.

S0185.name: SEASHARPEE
S0185.summary: SEASHARPEE is a Web shell that has been used by OilRig.

S0186.name: DownPaper
S0186.summary: DownPaper is a backdoor Trojan; its main functionality is to download and run second stage malware.

S0187.name: Daserf
S0187.summary: Daserf is a backdoor that has been used to spy on and steal from Japanese, South Korean, Russian, Singaporean, and Chinese victims. Researchers have identified versions written in both Visual C and Delphi.

S0188.name: Starloader
S0188.summary: Starloader is a loader component that has been observed loading Felismus and associated tools.

S0189.name: ISMInjector
S0189.summary: ISMInjector is a Trojan used to install another OilRig backdoor, ISMAgent.

S0190.name: BITSAdmin
S0190.summary: BITSAdmin is a command line tool used to create and manage BITS Jobs.

S0191.name: Winexe
S0191.summary: Winexe is a lightweight, open source tool similar to PsExec designed to allow system administrators to execute commands on remote servers. Winexe is unique in that it is a GNU/Linux based client.

S0192.name: Pupy
S0192.summary: Pupy is an open source, cross-platform (Windows, Linux, OSX, Android) remote administration and post-exploitation tool. It is written in Python and can be generated as a payload in several different ways (Windows exe, Python file, PowerShell oneliner/file, Linux elf, APK, Rubber Ducky, etc.). Pupy is publicly available on GitHub.

S0193.name: Forfiles
S0193.summary: Forfiles is a Windows utility commonly used in batch jobs to execute commands on one or more selected files or directories (ex: list all directories in a drive, read the first line of all files created yesterday, etc.). Forfiles can be executed from either the command line, Run window, or batch files/scripts.

S0194.name: PowerSploit
S0194.summary: PowerSploit is an open source, offensive security framework comprised of PowerShell modules and scripts that perform a wide range of tasks related to penetration testing such as code execution, persistence, bypassing anti-virus, recon, and exfiltration.

S0195.name: SDelete
S0195.summary: SDelete is an application that securely deletes data in a way that makes it unrecoverable. It is part of the Microsoft Sysinternals suite of tools.

S0196.name: PUNCHBUGGY
S0196.summary: PUNCHBUGGY is a backdoor malware used by FIN8 that has been observed targeting POS networks in the hospitality industry.

S0197.name: PUNCHTRACK
S0197.summary: PUNCHTRACK is non-persistent point of sale (POS) system malware utilized by FIN8 to scrape payment card data.

S0198.name: NETWIRE
S0198.summary: NETWIRE is a publicly available, multiplatform remote administration tool (RAT) that has been used by criminal and APT groups since at least 2012.

S0199.name: TURNEDUP
S0199.summary: TURNEDUP is a non-public backdoor. It has been dropped by APT33's StoneDrill malware.

S0200.name: Dipsind
S0200.summary: Dipsind is a malware family of backdoors that appear to be used exclusively by PLATINUM.

S0201.name: JPIN
S0201.summary: JPIN is a custom-built backdoor family used by PLATINUM. Evidence suggests developers of JPIN and Dipsind code bases were related in some way.

S0202.name: adbupd
S0202.summary: adbupd is a backdoor used by PLATINUM that is similar to Dipsind.

S0203.name: Hydraq
S0203.summary: Hydraq is a data-theft trojan first used by Elderwood in the 2009 Google intrusion known as Operation Aurora, though variations of this trojan have been used in more recent campaigns by other Chinese actors, possibly including APT17.

S0204.name: Briba
S0204.summary: Briba is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor and download files on to compromised hosts.

S0205.name: Naid
S0205.summary: Naid is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

S0206.name: Wiarp
S0206.summary: Wiarp is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

S0207.name: Vasport
S0207.summary: Vasport is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

S0208.name: Pasam
S0208.summary: Pasam is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

S0210.name: Nerex
S0210.summary: Nerex is a Trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

S0211.name: Linfo
S0211.summary: Linfo is a rootkit trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts.

S0212.name: CORALDECK
S0212.summary: CORALDECK is an exfiltration tool used by APT37.

S0213.name: DOGCALL
S0213.summary: DOGCALL is a backdoor used by APT37 that has been used to target South Korean government and military organizations in 2017. It is typically dropped using a Hangul Word Processor (HWP) exploit.

S0214.name: HAPPYWORK
S0214.summary: HAPPYWORK is a downloader used by APT37 to target South Korean government and financial victims in November 2016.

S0215.name: KARAE
S0215.summary: KARAE is a backdoor typically used by APT37 as first-stage malware.

S0216.name: POORAIM
S0216.summary: POORAIM is a backdoor used by APT37 in campaigns since at least 2014.

S0217.name: SHUTTERSPEED
S0217.summary: SHUTTERSPEED is a backdoor used by APT37.

S0218.name: SLOWDRIFT
S0218.summary: SLOWDRIFT is a backdoor used by APT37 against academic and strategic victims in South Korea.

S0219.name: WINERACK
S0219.summary: WINERACK is a backdoor used by APT37.

S0220.name: Chaos
S0220.summary: Chaos is Linux malware that compromises systems by brute force attacks against SSH services. Once installed, it provides a reverse shell to its controllers, triggered by unsolicited packets.

S0221.name: Umbreon
S0221.summary: A Linux rootkit that provides backdoor access and hides from defenders.

S0222.name: CCBkdr
S0222.summary: CCBkdr is malware that was injected into a signed version of CCleaner and distributed from CCleaner's distribution website.

S0223.name: POWERSTATS
S0223.summary: POWERSTATS is a PowerShell-based first stage backdoor used by MuddyWater.

S0224.name: Havij
S0224.summary: Havij is an automatic SQL Injection tool distributed by the Iranian ITSecTeam security company. Havij has been used by penetration testers and adversaries.

S0225.name: sqlmap
S0225.summary: sqlmap is an open source penetration testing tool that can be used to automate the process of detecting and exploiting SQL injection flaws.

S0226.name: Smoke Loader
S0226.summary: Smoke Loader is a malicious bot application that can be used to load other malware.

S0227.name: spwebmember
S0227.summary: spwebmember is a Microsoft SharePoint enumeration and data dumping tool written in .NET.

S0228.name: NanHaiShu
S0228.summary: NanHaiShu is a remote access tool and JScript backdoor used by Leviathan. NanHaiShu has been used to target government and private-sector organizations that have relations to the South China Sea dispute.

S0229.name: Orz
S0229.summary: Orz is a custom JavaScript backdoor used by Leviathan. It was observed being used in 2014 as well as in August 2017 when it was dropped by Microsoft Publisher files.

S0230.name: ZeroT
S0230.summary: ZeroT is a Trojan used by TA459, often in conjunction with PlugX.

S0231.name: Invoke-PSImage
S0231.summary: Invoke-PSImage takes a PowerShell script and embeds the bytes of the script into the pixels of a PNG image. It generates a one liner for executing either from a file of from the web. Example of usage is embedding the PowerShell code from the Invoke-Mimikatz module and embed it into an image file.

S0232.name: HOMEFRY
S0232.summary: HOMEFRY is a 64-bit Windows password dumper/cracker that has previously been used in conjunction with other Leviathan backdoors.

S0233.name: MURKYTOP
S0233.summary: MURKYTOP is a reconnaissance tool used by Leviathan.

S0234.name: Bandook
S0234.summary: Bandook is a commercially available RAT, written in Delphi and C++, that has been available since at least 2007. It has been used against government, financial, energy, healthcare, education, IT, and legal organizations in the US, South America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. Bandook has been used by Dark Caracal, as well as in a separate campaign referred to as "Operation Manul".

S0235.name: CrossRAT
S0235.summary: CrossRAT is a cross platform RAT.

S0236.name: Kwampirs
S0236.summary: Kwampirs is a backdoor Trojan used by Orangeworm. Kwampirs has been found on machines which had software installed for the use and control of high-tech imaging devices such as X-Ray and MRI machines. Kwampirs has multiple technical overlaps with Shamoon based on reverse engineering analysis.

S0237.name: GravityRAT
S0237.summary: GravityRAT is a remote access tool (RAT) and has been in ongoing development since 2016. The actor behind the tool remains unknown, but two usernames have been recovered that link to the author, which are "TheMartian" and "The Invincible." According to the National Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) of India, the malware has been identified in attacks against organization and entities in India.

S0238.name: Proxysvc
S0238.summary: Proxysvc is a malicious DLL used by Lazarus Group in a campaign known as Operation GhostSecret. It has appeared to be operating undetected since 2017 and was mostly observed in higher education organizations. The goal of Proxysvc is to deliver additional payloads to the target and to maintain control for the attacker. It is in the form of a DLL that can also be executed as a standalone process.

S0239.name: Bankshot
S0239.summary: Bankshot is a remote access tool (RAT) that was first reported by the Department of Homeland Security in December of 2017. In 2018, Lazarus Group used the Bankshot implant in attacks against the Turkish financial sector.

S0240.name: ROKRAT
S0240.summary: ROKRAT is a cloud-based remote access tool (RAT) used by APT37 to target victims in South Korea. APT37 has used ROKRAT during several campaigns from 2016 through 2021.

S0241.name: RATANKBA
S0241.summary: RATANKBA is a remote controller tool used by Lazarus Group. RATANKBA has been used in attacks targeting financial institutions in Poland, Mexico, Uruguay, the United Kingdom, and Chile. It was also seen used against organizations related to telecommunications, management consulting, information technology, insurance, aviation, and education.

S0242.name: SynAck
S0242.summary: SynAck is variant of Trojan ransomware targeting mainly English-speaking users since at least fall 2017.

S0243.name: DealersChoice
S0243.summary: DealersChoice is a Flash exploitation framework used by APT28.

S0244.name: Comnie
S0244.summary: Comnie is a remote backdoor which has been used in attacks in East Asia.

S0245.name: BADCALL
S0245.summary: BADCALL is a Trojan malware variant used by the group Lazarus Group.

S0246.name: HARDRAIN
S0246.summary: HARDRAIN is a Trojan malware variant reportedly used by the North Korean government.

S0247.name: NavRAT
S0247.summary: NavRAT is a remote access tool designed to upload, download, and execute files. It has been observed in attacks targeting South Korea.

S0248.name: yty
S0248.summary: yty is a modular, plugin-based malware framework. The components of the framework are written in a variety of programming languages.

S0249.name: Gold Dragon
S0249.summary: Gold Dragon is a Korean-language, data gathering implant that was first observed in the wild in South Korea in July 2017. Gold Dragon was used along with Brave Prince and RunningRAT in operations targeting organizations associated with the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics.

S0250.name: Koadic
S0250.summary: Koadic is a Windows post-exploitation framework and penetration testing tool that is publicly available on GitHub. Koadic has several options for staging payloads and creating implants, and performs most of its operations using Windows Script Host.

S0251.name: Zebrocy
S0251.summary: Zebrocy is a Trojan that has been used by APT28 since at least November 2015. The malware comes in several programming language variants, including C++, Delphi, AutoIt, C#, VB.NET, and Golang.

S0252.name: Brave Prince
S0252.summary: Brave Prince is a Korean-language implant that was first observed in the wild in December 2017. It contains similar code and behavior to Gold Dragon, and was seen along with Gold Dragon and RunningRAT in operations surrounding the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics.

S0253.name: RunningRAT
S0253.summary: RunningRAT is a remote access tool that appeared in operations surrounding the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics along with Gold Dragon and Brave Prince.

S0254.name: PLAINTEE
S0254.summary: PLAINTEE is a malware sample that has been used by Rancor in targeted attacks in Singapore and Cambodia.

S0255.name: DDKONG
S0255.summary: DDKONG is a malware sample that was part of a campaign by Rancor. DDKONG was first seen used in February 2017.

S0256.name: Mosquito
S0256.summary: Mosquito is a Win32 backdoor that has been used by Turla. Mosquito is made up of three parts: the installer, the launcher, and the backdoor. The main backdoor is called CommanderDLL and is launched by the loader program.

S0257.name: VERMIN
S0257.summary: VERMIN is a remote access tool written in the Microsoft .NET framework. It is mostly composed of original code, but also has some open source code.

S0258.name: RGDoor
S0258.summary: RGDoor is a malicious Internet Information Services (IIS) backdoor developed in the C++ language. RGDoor has been seen deployed on webservers belonging to the Middle East government organizations. RGDoor provides backdoor access to compromised IIS servers.

S0259.name: InnaputRAT
S0259.summary: InnaputRAT is a remote access tool that can exfiltrate files from a victim’s machine. InnaputRAT has been seen out in the wild since 2016.

S0260.name: InvisiMole
S0260.summary: InvisiMole is a modular spyware program that has been used by the InvisiMole Group since at least 2013. InvisiMole has two backdoor modules called RC2FM and RC2CL that are used to perform post-exploitation activities. It has been discovered on compromised victims in the Ukraine and Russia. Gamaredon Group infrastructure has been used to download and execute InvisiMole against a small number of victims.

S0261.name: Catchamas
S0261.summary: Catchamas is a Windows Trojan that steals information from compromised systems.

S0262.name: QuasarRAT
S0262.summary: QuasarRAT is an open-source, remote access tool that has been publicly available on GitHub since at least 2014. QuasarRAT is developed in the C# language.

S0263.name: TYPEFRAME
S0263.summary: TYPEFRAME is a remote access tool that has been used by Lazarus Group.

S0264.name: OopsIE
S0264.summary: OopsIE is a Trojan used by OilRig to remotely execute commands as well as upload/download files to/from victims.

S0265.name: Kazuar
S0265.summary: Kazuar is a fully featured, multi-platform backdoor Trojan written using the Microsoft .NET framework.

S0266.name: TrickBot
S0266.summary: TrickBot is a Trojan spyware program written in C++ that first emerged in September 2016 as a possible successor to Dyre. TrickBot was developed and initially used by Wizard Spider for targeting banking sites in North America, Australia, and throughout Europe; it has since been used against all sectors worldwide as part of "big game hunting" ransomware campaigns.

S0267.name: FELIXROOT
S0267.summary: FELIXROOT is a backdoor that has been used to target Ukrainian victims.

S0268.name: Bisonal
S0268.summary: Bisonal is a remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by Tonto Team against public and private sector organizations in Russia, South Korea, and Japan since at least December 2010.

S0269.name: QUADAGENT
S0269.summary: QUADAGENT is a PowerShell backdoor used by OilRig.

S0270.name: RogueRobin
S0270.summary: RogueRobin is a payload used by DarkHydrus that has been developed in PowerShell and C#.

S0271.name: KEYMARBLE
S0271.summary: KEYMARBLE is a Trojan that has reportedly been used by the North Korean government.

S0272.name: NDiskMonitor
S0272.summary: NDiskMonitor is a custom backdoor written in .NET that appears to be unique to Patchwork.

S0273.name: Socksbot
S0273.summary: Socksbot is a backdoor that abuses Socket Secure (SOCKS) proxies.

S0274.name: Calisto
S0274.summary: Calisto is a macOS Trojan that opens a backdoor on the compromised machine. Calisto is believed to have first been developed in 2016.

S0275.name: UPPERCUT
S0275.summary: UPPERCUT is a 32-bit HTTP-based backdoor that has been used by menuPass since at least 2017. Once thought to be exclusive to menuPass, UPPERCUT was also observed being used by menuPass-associated MirrorFace during Operation AkaiRyū.

S0276.name: Keydnap
S0276.summary: This piece of malware steals the content of the user's keychain while maintaining a permanent backdoor .

S0277.name: FruitFly
S0277.summary: FruitFly is designed to spy on mac users .

S0278.name: iKitten
S0278.summary: iKitten is a macOS exfiltration agent .

S0279.name: Proton
S0279.summary: Proton is a macOS backdoor focusing on data theft and credential access .

S0280.name: MirageFox
S0280.summary: MirageFox is a remote access tool used against Windows systems. It appears to be an upgraded version of a tool known as Mirage, which is a RAT believed to originate in 2012.

S0281.name: Dok
S0281.summary: Dok is a Trojan application disguised as a .zip file that is able to collect user credentials and install a malicious proxy server to redirect a user's network traffic (i.e. Adversary-in-the-Middle).

S0282.name: MacSpy
S0282.summary: MacSpy is a malware-as-a-service offered on the darkweb .

S0283.name: jRAT
S0283.summary: jRAT is a cross-platform, Java-based backdoor originally available for purchase in 2012. Variants of jRAT have been distributed via a software-as-a-service platform, similar to an online subscription model.

S0284.name: More_eggs
S0284.summary: More_eggs is a JScript backdoor used by Cobalt Group and FIN6. Its name was given based on the variable "More_eggs" being present in its code. There are at least two different versions of the backdoor being used, version 2.0 and version 4.4.

S0330.name: Zeus Panda
S0330.summary: Zeus Panda is a Trojan designed to steal banking information and other sensitive credentials for exfiltration. Zeus Panda’s original source code was leaked in 2011, allowing threat actors to use its source code as a basis for new malware variants. It is mainly used to target Windows operating systems ranging from Windows XP through Windows 10.

S0331.name: Agent Tesla
S0331.summary: Agent Tesla is a spyware Trojan written for the .NET framework that has been observed since at least 2014.

S0332.name: Remcos
S0332.summary: Remcos is a closed-source tool that is marketed as a remote control and surveillance software by a company called Breaking Security. Remcos has been observed being used in malware campaigns.

S0333.name: UBoatRAT
S0333.summary: UBoatRAT is a remote access tool that was identified in May 2017.

S0334.name: DarkComet
S0334.summary: DarkComet is a Windows remote administration tool and backdoor.

S0335.name: Carbon
S0335.summary: Carbon is a sophisticated, second-stage backdoor and framework that can be used to steal sensitive information from victims. Carbon has been selectively used by Turla to target government and foreign affairs-related organizations in Central Asia.

S0336.name: NanoCore
S0336.summary: NanoCore is a modular remote access tool developed in .NET that can be used to spy on victims and steal information. It has been used by threat actors since 2013.

S0337.name: BadPatch
S0337.summary: BadPatch is a Windows Trojan that was used in a Gaza Hackers-linked campaign.

S0338.name: Cobian RAT
S0338.summary: Cobian RAT is a backdoor, remote access tool that has been observed since 2016.

S0339.name: Micropsia
S0339.summary: Micropsia is a remote access tool written in Delphi.

S0340.name: Octopus
S0340.summary: Octopus is a Windows Trojan written in the Delphi programming language that has been used by Nomadic Octopus to target government organizations in Central Asia since at least 2014.

S0341.name: Xbash
S0341.summary: Xbash is a malware family that has targeted Linux and Microsoft Windows servers. The malware has been tied to the Iron Group, a threat actor group known for previous ransomware attacks. Xbash was developed in Python and then converted into a self-contained Linux ELF executable by using PyInstaller.

S0342.name: GreyEnergy
S0342.summary: GreyEnergy is a backdoor written in C and compiled in Visual Studio. GreyEnergy shares similarities with the BlackEnergy malware and is thought to be the successor of it.

S0343.name: Exaramel for Windows
S0343.summary: Exaramel for Windows is a backdoor used for targeting Windows systems. The Linux version is tracked separately under Exaramel for Linux.

S0344.name: Azorult
S0344.summary: Azorult is a commercial Trojan that is used to steal information from compromised hosts. Azorult has been observed in the wild as early as 2016.

S0345.name: Seasalt
S0345.summary: Seasalt is malware that has been linked to APT1's 2010 operations. It shares some code similarities with OceanSalt.

S0346.name: OceanSalt
S0346.summary: OceanSalt is a Trojan that was used in a campaign targeting victims in South Korea, United States, and Canada. OceanSalt shares code similarity with SpyNote RAT, which has been linked to APT1.

S0347.name: AuditCred
S0347.summary: AuditCred is a malicious DLL that has been used by Lazarus Group during their 2018 attacks.

S0348.name: Cardinal RAT
S0348.summary: Cardinal RAT is a potentially low volume remote access trojan (RAT) observed since December 2015. Cardinal RAT is notable for its unique utilization of uncompiled C# source code and the Microsoft Windows built-in csc.exe compiler.

S0349.name: LaZagne
S0349.summary: LaZagne is a post-exploitation, open-source tool used to recover stored passwords on a system. It has modules for Windows, Linux, and OSX, but is mainly focused on Windows systems. LaZagne is publicly available on GitHub.

S0350.name: zwShell
S0350.summary: zwShell is a remote access tool (RAT) written in Delphi that has been seen in the wild since the spring of 2010 and used by threat actors during Night Dragon.

S0351.name: Cannon
S0351.summary: Cannon is a Trojan with variants written in C# and Delphi. It was first observed in April 2018.

S0352.name: OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D
S0352.summary: OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D is a macOS backdoor used by APT32. First discovered in 2015, APT32 has continued to make improvements using a plugin architecture to extend capabilities, specifically using `.dylib` files. OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D can also determine it's permission level and execute according to access type (`root` or `user`).

S0353.name: NOKKI
S0353.summary: NOKKI is a modular remote access tool. The earliest observed attack using NOKKI was in January 2018. NOKKI has significant code overlap with the KONNI malware family. There is some evidence potentially linking NOKKI to APT37.

S0354.name: Denis
S0354.summary: Denis is a Windows backdoor and Trojan used by APT32. Denis shares several similarities to the SOUNDBITE backdoor and has been used in conjunction with the Goopy backdoor.

S0355.name: Final1stspy
S0355.summary: Final1stspy is a dropper family that has been used to deliver DOGCALL.

S0356.name: KONNI
S0356.summary: KONNI is a remote access tool that security researchers assess has been used by North Korean cyber actors since at least 2014. KONNI has significant code overlap with the NOKKI malware family, and has been linked to several suspected North Korean campaigns targeting political organizations in Russia, East Asia, Europe and the Middle East; there is some evidence potentially linking KONNI to APT37.

S0357.name: Impacket
S0357.summary: Impacket is an open source collection of modules written in Python for programmatically constructing and manipulating network protocols. Impacket contains several tools for remote service execution, Kerberos manipulation, Windows credential dumping, packet sniffing, and relay attacks.

S0358.name: Ruler
S0358.summary: Ruler is a tool to abuse Microsoft Exchange services. It is publicly available on GitHub and the tool is executed via the command line. The creators of Ruler have also released a defensive tool, NotRuler, to detect its usage.

S0359.name: Nltest
S0359.summary: Nltest is a Windows command-line utility used to list domain controllers and enumerate domain trusts.

S0360.name: BONDUPDATER
S0360.summary: BONDUPDATER is a PowerShell backdoor used by OilRig. It was first observed in November 2017 during targeting of a Middle Eastern government organization, and an updated version was observed in August 2018 being used to target a government organization with spearphishing emails.

S0361.name: Expand
S0361.summary: Expand is a Windows utility used to expand one or more compressed CAB files. It has been used by BBSRAT to decompress a CAB file into executable content.

S0362.name: Linux Rabbit
S0362.summary: Linux Rabbit is malware that targeted Linux servers and IoT devices in a campaign lasting from August to October 2018. It shares code with another strain of malware known as Rabbot. The goal of the campaign was to install cryptocurrency miners onto the targeted servers and devices.

S0363.name: Empire
S0363.summary: Empire is an open-source, cross-platform remote administration and post-exploitation framework that is publicly available on GitHub. While the tool itself is primarily written in Python, the post-exploitation agents are written in pure PowerShell for Windows and Python for Linux/macOS. Empire was one of five tools singled out by a joint report on public hacking tools being widely used by adversaries.

S0364.name: RawDisk
S0364.summary: RawDisk is a legitimate commercial driver from the EldoS Corporation that is used for interacting with files, disks, and partitions. The driver allows for direct modification of data on a local computer's hard drive. In some cases, the tool can enact these raw disk modifications from user-mode processes, circumventing Windows operating system security features.

S0365.name: Olympic Destroyer
S0365.summary: Olympic Destroyer is malware that was used by Sandworm Team against the 2018 Winter Olympics, held in Pyeongchang, South Korea. The main purpose of the malware was to render infected computer systems inoperable. The malware leverages various native Windows utilities and API calls to carry out its destructive tasks.

S0366.name: WannaCry
S0366.summary: WannaCry is ransomware that was first seen in a global attack during May 2017, which affected more than 150 countries. It contains worm-like features to spread itself across a computer network using the SMBv1 exploit EternalBlue.

S0367.name: Emotet
S0367.summary: Emotet is a modular malware variant which is primarily used as a downloader for other malware variants such as TrickBot and IcedID. Emotet first emerged in June 2014, initially targeting the financial sector, and has expanded to multiple verticals over time.

S0368.name: NotPetya
S0368.summary: NotPetya is malware that was used by Sandworm Team in a worldwide attack starting on June 27, 2017. While NotPetya appears as a form of ransomware, its main purpose was to destroy data and disk structures on compromised systems; the attackers never intended to make the encrypted data recoverable. As such, NotPetya may be more appropriately thought of as a form of wiper malware.

S0369.name: CoinTicker
S0369.summary: CoinTicker is a malicious application that poses as a cryptocurrency price ticker and installs components of the open source backdoors EvilOSX and EggShell.

S0370.name: SamSam
S0370.summary: SamSam is ransomware that appeared in early 2016. Unlike some ransomware, its variants have required operators to manually interact with the malware to execute some of its core components.

S0371.name: POWERTON
S0371.summary: POWERTON is a custom PowerShell backdoor first observed in 2018. It has typically been deployed as a late-stage backdoor by APT33. At least two variants of the backdoor have been identified, with the later version containing improved functionality.

S0372.name: LockerGoga
S0372.summary: LockerGoga is ransomware that was first reported in January 2019, and has been tied to various attacks on European companies, including industrial and manufacturing firms.

S0373.name: Astaroth
S0373.summary: Astaroth is a Trojan and information stealer known to affect companies in Europe, Brazil, and throughout Latin America. It has been known publicly since at least late 2017.

S0374.name: SpeakUp
S0374.summary: SpeakUp is a Trojan backdoor that targets both Linux and OSX devices. It was first observed in January 2019.

S0375.name: Remexi
S0375.summary: Remexi is a Windows-based Trojan that was developed in the C programming language.

S0376.name: HOPLIGHT
S0376.summary: HOPLIGHT is a backdoor Trojan that has reportedly been used by the North Korean government.

S0377.name: Ebury
S0377.summary: Ebury is an OpenSSH backdoor and credential stealer targeting Linux servers and container hosts developed by Windigo. Ebury is primarily installed through modifying shared libraries (`.so` files) executed by the legitimate OpenSSH program. First seen in 2009, Ebury has been used to maintain a botnet of servers, deploy additional malware, and steal cryptocurrency wallets, credentials, and credit card details.

S0378.name: PoshC2
S0378.summary: PoshC2 is an open source remote administration and post-exploitation framework that is publicly available on GitHub. The server-side components of the tool are primarily written in Python, while the implants are written in PowerShell. Although PoshC2 is primarily focused on Windows implantation, it does contain a basic Python dropper for Linux/macOS.

S0379.name: Revenge RAT
S0379.summary: Revenge RAT is a freely available remote access tool written in .NET (C#).

S0380.name: StoneDrill
S0380.summary: StoneDrill is wiper malware discovered in destructive campaigns against both Middle Eastern and European targets in association with APT33.

S0381.name: FlawedAmmyy
S0381.summary: FlawedAmmyy is a remote access tool (RAT) that was first seen in early 2016. The code for FlawedAmmyy was based on leaked source code for a version of Ammyy Admin, a remote access software.

S0382.name: ServHelper
S0382.summary: ServHelper is a backdoor first observed in late 2018. The backdoor is written in Delphi and is typically delivered as a DLL file.

S0383.name: FlawedGrace
S0383.summary: FlawedGrace is a fully featured remote access tool (RAT) written in C++ that was first observed in late 2017.

S0384.name: Dridex
S0384.summary: Dridex is a prolific banking Trojan that first appeared in 2014. By December 2019, the US Treasury estimated Dridex had infected computers in hundreds of banks and financial institutions in over 40 countries, leading to more than $100 million in theft. Dridex was created from the source code of the Bugat banking Trojan (also known as Cridex).

S0385.name: njRAT
S0385.summary: njRAT is a remote access tool (RAT) that was first observed in 2012. It has been used by threat actors in the Middle East.

S0386.name: Ursnif
S0386.summary: Ursnif is a banking trojan and variant of the Gozi malware observed being spread through various automated exploit kits, Spearphishing Attachments, and malicious links. Ursnif is associated primarily with data theft, but variants also include components (backdoors, spyware, file injectors, etc.) capable of a wide variety of behaviors.

S0387.name: KeyBoy
S0387.summary: KeyBoy is malware that has been used in targeted campaigns against members of the Tibetan Parliament in 2016.

S0388.name: YAHOYAH
S0388.summary: YAHOYAH is a Trojan used by Tropic Trooper as a second-stage backdoor.

S0389.name: JCry
S0389.summary: JCry is ransomware written in Go. It was identified as apart of the #OpJerusalem 2019 campaign.

S0390.name: SQLRat
S0390.summary: SQLRat is malware that executes SQL scripts to avoid leaving traditional host artifacts. FIN7 has been observed using it.

S0391.name: HAWKBALL
S0391.summary: HAWKBALL is a backdoor that was observed in targeting of the government sector in Central Asia.

S0393.name: PowerStallion
S0393.summary: PowerStallion is a lightweight PowerShell backdoor used by Turla, possibly as a recovery access tool to install other backdoors.

S0394.name: HiddenWasp
S0394.summary: HiddenWasp is a Linux-based Trojan used to target systems for remote control. It comes in the form of a statically linked ELF binary with stdlibc++.

S0395.name: LightNeuron
S0395.summary: LightNeuron is a sophisticated backdoor that has targeted Microsoft Exchange servers since at least 2014. LightNeuron has been used by Turla to target diplomatic and foreign affairs-related organizations. The presence of certain strings in the malware suggests a Linux variant of LightNeuron exists.

S0396.name: EvilBunny
S0396.summary: EvilBunny is a C++ malware sample observed since 2011 that was designed to be a execution platform for Lua scripts.

S0397.name: LoJax
S0397.summary: LoJax is a UEFI rootkit used by APT28 to persist remote access software on targeted systems.

S0398.name: HyperBro
S0398.summary: HyperBro is a custom in-memory backdoor used by Threat Group-3390.

S0400.name: RobbinHood
S0400.summary: RobbinHood is ransomware that was first observed being used in an attack against the Baltimore city government's computer network.

S0401.name: Exaramel for Linux
S0401.summary: Exaramel for Linux is a backdoor written in the Go Programming Language and compiled as a 64-bit ELF binary. The Windows version is tracked separately under Exaramel for Windows.

S0402.name: OSX/Shlayer
S0402.summary: OSX/Shlayer is a Trojan designed to install adware on macOS that was first discovered in 2018.

S0404.name: esentutl
S0404.summary: esentutl is a command-line tool that provides database utilities for the Windows Extensible Storage Engine.

S0409.name: Machete
S0409.summary: Machete is a cyber espionage toolset used by Machete. It is a Python-based backdoor targeting Windows machines that was first observed in 2010.

S0410.name: Fysbis
S0410.summary: Fysbis is a Linux-based backdoor used by APT28 that dates back to at least 2014.

S0412.name: ZxShell
S0412.summary: ZxShell is a remote administration tool and backdoor that can be downloaded from the Internet, particularly from Chinese hacker websites. It has been used since at least 2004.

S0413.name: MailSniper
S0413.summary: MailSniper is a penetration testing tool for searching through email in a Microsoft Exchange environment for specific terms (passwords, insider intel, network architecture information, etc.). It can be used by a non-administrative user to search their own email, or by an Exchange administrator to search the mailboxes of every user in a domain.

S0414.name: BabyShark
S0414.summary: BabyShark is a Microsoft Visual Basic (VB) script-based malware family that is believed to be associated with several North Korean campaigns.

S0415.name: BOOSTWRITE
S0415.summary: BOOSTWRITE is a loader crafted to be launched via abuse of the DLL search order of applications used by FIN7.

S0416.name: RDFSNIFFER
S0416.summary: RDFSNIFFER is a module loaded by BOOSTWRITE which allows an attacker to monitor and tamper with legitimate connections made via an application designed to provide visibility and system management capabilities to remote IT techs.

S0417.name: GRIFFON
S0417.summary: GRIFFON is a JavaScript backdoor used by FIN7.

S0428.name: PoetRAT
S0428.summary: PoetRAT is a remote access trojan (RAT) that was first identified in April 2020. PoetRAT has been used in multiple campaigns against the private and public sectors in Azerbaijan, including ICS and SCADA systems in the energy sector. The STIBNITE activity group has been observed using the malware. PoetRAT derived its name from references in the code to poet William Shakespeare.

S0430.name: Winnti for Linux
S0430.summary: Winnti for Linux is a trojan, seen since at least 2015, designed specifically for targeting Linux systems. Reporting indicates the winnti malware family is shared across a number of actors including Winnti Group. The Windows variant is tracked separately under Winnti for Windows.

S0431.name: HotCroissant
S0431.summary: HotCroissant is a remote access trojan (RAT) attributed by U.S. government entities to malicious North Korean government cyber activity, tracked collectively as HIDDEN COBRA. HotCroissant shares numerous code similarities with Rifdoor.

S0433.name: Rifdoor
S0433.summary: Rifdoor is a remote access trojan (RAT) that shares numerous code similarities with HotCroissant.

S0434.name: Imminent Monitor
S0434.summary: Imminent Monitor was a commodity remote access tool (RAT) offered for sale from 2012 until 2019, when an operation was conducted to take down the Imminent Monitor infrastructure. Various cracked versions and variations of this RAT are still in circulation.

S0435.name: PLEAD
S0435.summary: PLEAD is a remote access tool (RAT) and downloader used by BlackTech in targeted attacks in East Asia including Taiwan, Japan, and Hong Kong. PLEAD has also been referred to as TSCookie, though more recent reporting indicates likely separation between the two. PLEAD was observed in use as early as March 2017.

S0436.name: TSCookie
S0436.summary: TSCookie is a remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by BlackTech in campaigns against Japanese targets.. TSCookie has been referred to as PLEAD though more recent reporting indicates a separation between the two.

S0437.name: Kivars
S0437.summary: Kivars is a modular remote access tool (RAT), derived from the Bifrost RAT, that was used by BlackTech in a 2010 campaign.

S0438.name: Attor
S0438.summary: Attor is a Windows-based espionage platform that has been seen in use since 2013. Attor has a loadable plugin architecture to customize functionality for specific targets.

S0439.name: Okrum
S0439.summary: Okrum is a Windows backdoor that has been seen in use since December 2016 with strong links to Ke3chang.

S0441.name: PowerShower
S0441.summary: PowerShower is a PowerShell backdoor used by Inception for initial reconnaissance and to download and execute second stage payloads.

S0442.name: VBShower
S0442.summary: VBShower is a backdoor that has been used by Inception since at least 2019. VBShower has been used as a downloader for second stage payloads, including PowerShower.

S0443.name: MESSAGETAP
S0443.summary: MESSAGETAP is a data mining malware family deployed by APT41 into telecommunications networks to monitor and save SMS traffic from specific phone numbers, IMSI numbers, or that contain specific keywords.

S0444.name: ShimRat
S0444.summary: ShimRat has been used by the suspected China-based adversary Mofang in campaigns targeting multiple countries and sectors including government, military, critical infrastructure, automobile, and weapons development. The name "ShimRat" comes from the malware's extensive use of Windows Application Shimming to maintain persistence.

S0445.name: ShimRatReporter
S0445.summary: ShimRatReporter is a tool used by suspected Chinese adversary Mofang to automatically conduct initial discovery. The details from this discovery are used to customize follow-on payloads (such as ShimRat) as well as set up faux infrastructure which mimics the adversary's targets.

S0446.name: Ryuk
S0446.summary: Ryuk is a ransomware designed to target enterprise environments that has been used in attacks since at least 2018. Ryuk shares code similarities with Hermes ransomware.

S0447.name: Lokibot
S0447.summary: Lokibot is a widely distributed information stealer that was first reported in 2015. It is designed to steal sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, cryptocurrency wallets, and other credentials. Lokibot can also create a backdoor into infected systems to allow an attacker to install additional payloads.

S0448.name: Rising Sun
S0448.summary: Rising Sun is a modular backdoor that was used extensively in Operation Sharpshooter between 2017 and 2019. Rising Sun infected at least 87 organizations around the world, including nuclear, defense, energy, and financial service companies. Security researchers assessed Rising Sun included some source code from Lazarus Group's Trojan Duuzer.

S0449.name: Maze
S0449.summary: Maze ransomware, previously known as "ChaCha", was discovered in May 2019. In addition to encrypting files on victim machines for impact, Maze operators conduct information stealing campaigns prior to encryption and post the information online to extort affected companies.

S0450.name: SHARPSTATS
S0450.summary: SHARPSTATS is a .NET backdoor used by MuddyWater since at least 2019.

S0451.name: LoudMiner
S0451.summary: LoudMiner is a cryptocurrency miner which uses virtualization software to siphon system resources. The miner has been bundled with pirated copies of Virtual Studio Technology (VST) for Windows and macOS.

S0452.name: USBferry
S0452.summary: USBferry is an information stealing malware and has been used by Tropic Trooper in targeted attacks against Taiwanese and Philippine air-gapped military environments. USBferry shares an overlapping codebase with YAHOYAH, though it has several features which makes it a distinct piece of malware.

S0453.name: Pony
S0453.summary: Pony is a credential stealing malware, though has also been used among adversaries for its downloader capabilities. The source code for Pony Loader 1.0 and 2.0 were leaked online, leading to their use by various threat actors.

S0454.name: Cadelspy
S0454.summary: Cadelspy is a backdoor that has been used by APT39.

S0455.name: Metamorfo
S0455.summary: Metamorfo is a Latin-American banking trojan operated by a Brazilian cybercrime group that has been active since at least April 2018. The group focuses on targeting banks and cryptocurrency services in Brazil and Mexico.

S0456.name: Aria-body
S0456.summary: Aria-body is a custom backdoor that has been used by Naikon since approximately 2017.

S0457.name: Netwalker
S0457.summary: Netwalker is fileless ransomware written in PowerShell and executed directly in memory.

S0458.name: Ramsay
S0458.summary: Ramsay is an information stealing malware framework designed to collect and exfiltrate sensitive documents, including from air-gapped systems. Researchers have identified overlaps between Ramsay and the Darkhotel-associated Retro malware.

S0459.name: MechaFlounder
S0459.summary: MechaFlounder is a python-based remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by APT39. The payload uses a combination of actor developed code and code snippets freely available online in development communities.

S0460.name: Get2
S0460.summary: Get2 is a downloader written in C++ that has been used by TA505 to deliver FlawedGrace, FlawedAmmyy, Snatch and SDBbot.

S0461.name: SDBbot
S0461.summary: SDBbot is a backdoor with installer and loader components that has been used by TA505 since at least 2019.

S0462.name: CARROTBAT
S0462.summary: CARROTBAT is a customized dropper that has been in use since at least 2017. CARROTBAT has been used to install SYSCON and has infrastructure overlap with KONNI.

S0464.name: SYSCON
S0464.summary: SYSCON is a backdoor that has been in use since at least 2017 and has been associated with campaigns involving North Korean themes. SYSCON has been delivered by the CARROTBALL and CARROTBAT droppers.

S0465.name: CARROTBALL
S0465.summary: CARROTBALL is an FTP downloader utility that has been in use since at least 2019. CARROTBALL has been used as a downloader to install SYSCON.

S0466.name: WindTail
S0466.summary: WindTail is a macOS surveillance implant used by Windshift. WindTail shares code similarities with Hack Back aka KitM OSX.

S0467.name: TajMahal
S0467.summary: TajMahal is a multifunctional spying framework that has been in use since at least 2014. TajMahal is comprised of two separate packages, named Tokyo and Yokohama, and can deploy up to 80 plugins.

S0468.name: Skidmap
S0468.summary: Skidmap is a kernel-mode rootkit used for cryptocurrency mining.

S0469.name: ABK
S0469.summary: ABK is a downloader that has been used by BRONZE BUTLER since at least 2019.

S0470.name: BBK
S0470.summary: BBK is a downloader that has been used by BRONZE BUTLER since at least 2019.

S0471.name: build_downer
S0471.summary: build_downer is a downloader that has been used by BRONZE BUTLER since at least 2019.

S0472.name: down_new
S0472.summary: down_new is a downloader that has been used by BRONZE BUTLER since at least 2019.

S0473.name: Avenger
S0473.summary: Avenger is a downloader that has been used by BRONZE BUTLER since at least 2019.

S0475.name: BackConfig
S0475.summary: BackConfig is a custom Trojan with a flexible plugin architecture that has been used by Patchwork.

S0476.name: Valak
S0476.summary: Valak is a multi-stage modular malware that can function as a standalone information stealer or downloader, first observed in 2019 targeting enterprises in the US and Germany.

S0477.name: Goopy
S0477.summary: Goopy is a Windows backdoor and Trojan used by APT32 and shares several similarities to another backdoor used by the group (Denis). Goopy is named for its impersonation of the legitimate Google Updater executable.

S0481.name: Ragnar Locker
S0481.summary: Ragnar Locker is a ransomware that has been in use since at least December 2019.

S0482.name: Bundlore
S0482.summary: Bundlore is adware written for macOS that has been in use since at least 2015. Though categorized as adware, Bundlore has many features associated with more traditional backdoors.

S0483.name: IcedID
S0483.summary: IcedID is a modular banking malware designed to steal financial information that has been observed in the wild since at least 2017. IcedID has been downloaded by Emotet in multiple campaigns.

S0484.name: Carberp
S0484.summary: Carberp is a credential and information stealing malware that has been active since at least 2009. Carberp's source code was leaked online in 2013, and subsequently used as the foundation for the Carbanak backdoor.

S0486.name: Bonadan
S0486.summary: Bonadan is a malicious version of OpenSSH which acts as a custom backdoor. Bonadan has been active since at least 2018 and combines a new cryptocurrency-mining module with the same credential-stealing module used by the Onderon family of backdoors.

S0487.name: Kessel
S0487.summary: Kessel is an advanced version of OpenSSH which acts as a custom backdoor, mainly acting to steal credentials and function as a bot. Kessel has been active since its C2 domain began resolving in August 2018.

S0488.name: CrackMapExec
